parsed.explanation: A trans visitor's sharpest exposure is at the border: national rules no longer issue X markers, and officers are directed to refuse cases where documents cast reasonable doubt on sex, with a possible lifetime fraud ineligibility finding; allied governments have issued travel advisories after detentions. Immigration custody is documented as abusive for trans detainees (forced labour, beatings, sexual abuse). Inside the state/province, a 2023 law permits excluding trans people from many state-run facilities, birth-marker changes are surgically gated, minors' gender-affirming care is banned, and schools must disclose. Offsetting: no criminalisation of trans identity or presentation, no documented anti-trans violence or police sweeps in this state/province, national hate-crime coverage, and litigation that has enjoined several orders. The regime is exclusionary, humiliating and costly rather than routinely lethal.

entry_documents.exposure: National passport agency no longer issues X markers and processes only M/F; officers instructed to refuse visa cases where documents or records cast doubt on sex, and to consider a permanent lifetime fraud ineligibility; trans athletes barred from women's competition; travellers report confiscated or blocked passports.
entry_documents.protection: Pre-existing X-marker passports remain valid until expiry; the policy is under challenge by a civil-liberties suit; a legal-aid FAQ documents options. No documented working remedy at the border itself.
entry_documents.interaction: This is the parent regime and reaches every visitor at every crossing regardless of the state/province's own birth-certificate rules; state marker-change law does not touch foreign-issued documents, but a state-banned marker heightens the appearance/paper mismatch a foreigner may present.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Trans men in immigration custody reported forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse; national corrections adopted a state model stripping hormones and imposing psychiatric substitution, and stopped reporting trans prisoner counts in 2025.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented for immigration detainees; consular access, counsel or oversight remedy for trans detainees is not documented as operating.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A document discrepancy at the border can move a visitor from screening into immigration detention, where the documented harm sits; the state/province's own criminal-trespass exposure (not documented here) is a lesser separate pathway.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: A 2023 state/province law effective 1 July explicitly allows restriction of transgender public-bathroom use in many state-run facilities; nationally 21 state/provinces ban identity-congruent facilities and 4 criminalise use with a trespass trigger (one arrest documented elsewhere).
federal_state_facilities.protection: No criminal bathroom statute is documented for this state/province; 29 state/provinces plus the capital district have no mapped ban; the documented statute's trespass paragraph only applies in specified states.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State-run buildings (capitols, agencies, schools, universities) are where a visitor's ID check and facility use converge; private venues are outside most bans, though 6 state/provinces reach private settings.

care_services.exposure: Gender-affirming care to minors is illegal in the state/province under a veto-proof 2023 law; proposed national rules would bar public reimbursement for under-18 care; health-agency vocabulary bans and grant revocations signal institutional hostility.
care_services.protection: Adult care is not documented as restricted in this state/province; a 2021 committee regulation bans conversion therapy by counsellors; some national orders have been enjoined.
care_services.interaction: A family seeking continuity of care for a trans minor confronts the state ban plus national funding and insurance rules simultaneously; an adult visitor's own prescription access is undocumented rather than protected.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: The May 2026 counterterrorism strategy prioritises 'neutralising' groups described as 'radically pro-transgender'; a December 2025 justice-department reward memorandum lists 'radical gender ideology' among extremist viewpoints; a January 2025 order directs investigation of schools and prosecution of teachers.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: The reward memo never makes gender ideology a reward criterion; the strategy disclaims targeting mere disagreement; several related orders are enjoined.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: This raises discovery salience and institutional willingness to scrutinise gender-nonconforming people, layering onto border and facility enforcement rather than operating as a standalone ban.

minors_guardians.exposure: A trans minor travelling with a guardian faces a state care ban, school rules forbidding required pronoun use and mandating parental disclosure, sports bans, and national subpoenas of hospital records for patients under 19; teachers using preferred names risk prosecution.
minors_guardians.protection: Several national executive orders are blocked or enjoined; the guardian is not documented as criminally liable for the child's identity; no state enforcement instance of the pronoun penalty is recorded.
minors_guardians.interaction: The exposure runs through the child's care and schooling and can pull the guardian into state inquiry; it compounds the adult visitor's own document and facility exposures on the same trip.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No dated anti-trans violence incident or police targeting is documented in this state/province; the state hate-crime statute excludes gender identity and the 2020 party platform opposed civil-rights protections.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crimes statute covers gender identity since 2009 and national prosecution is available; a 2022 poll records 78% support for an anti-discrimination law covering gender identity; no documented pattern of hostility toward trans visitors.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: State-level bias-crime coverage is absent, so recourse in this state/province depends on national prosecution, which is documented as available but not as exercised in a trans-specific case here.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Border refusals and lifetime ineligibility findings leave no documented effective appeal for a visitor mid-journey; at least eight regional governments and others issued advisories for trans travellers; the July 2026 assessment ranks the state/province among the worst for anti-trans legislation.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Active litigation against the passport policy; multiple executive orders blocked or enjoined; a legal-aid FAQ; national equality-law ruling of 2020 remains in force nationally.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies operate after the fact and unevenly: courts have checked some national orders but not the in-force passport and entry-screening guidance the traveller actually meets.

anchor_checks.comparison: Far safer than this anchor: no statute criminalises gender presentation here, no documented routine arrests of trans visitors at transit checks, no capital provision, no documented lethal or sexually abusive custody pattern applied to presentation cases as a matter of course, and detention abuse, while documented, is not shown to be the routine outcome of discovery.

Somewhat safer in kind: that anchor has an operative appearance-matching statute, weekly raids, detention, fines and police extortion. Here there is no criminalisation of presentation and no documented police shakedowns of trans people; but the border refusal with a possible lifetime fraud bar and the statutory facility exclusion are comparable or heavier state-imposed exposures, holding this case only modestly above it.

Broadly similar at the border: extended secondary screening on document divergence, discretionary refusal of admission, return transport, slow appeal. This case is worse because refusal can attach a permanent ineligibility finding, X markers cannot be issued, facility exclusion is statutory in the state/province, and immigration custody abuse is documented rather than absent.

Far below: that anchor recognises nonbinary passports, trains officers, provides legal aid in detention and promptly remedies errors. Here markers are restricted, officers are directed to doubt sex, and no working remedy for a refused visitor is documented, though litigation has checked some national orders.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime makes documents the dominant traveller exposure: national issuance rules narrow markers, and entry screening instructs officers to doubt sex where papers and records diverge, with refusal, stranding and a possible permanent ineligibility finding as the operative consequences, and immigration detention carrying documented beatings, forced labour and sexual abuse. Inside the state/province, a 2023 statute authorises excluding trans people from many state-run facilities, birth markers are surgically gated, and minors' care is banned with school disclosure obligations that pull guardians into inquiry. No trans-specific criminalisation, street campaign or documented anti-trans violence appears here, and national hate-crime coverage plus litigation provide partial recourse. The result is a high-friction, dignity-eroding regime with severe but not routine worst cases.
